children.title: Coercivity Modulo Invariances
children.top_down_role: Compactness after normalization by translations, constants, or other null directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional inequality certifying coercivity after removal of null directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\subset X\) be the invariant null space and suppose \[\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\le C(1+E(x)),\qquad F(x)\ge aE(x)-b,\quad a>0.\] Then every finite sublevel of \(F\) has bounded image in \(X/N\); equivalently, \(F\) is coercive modulo \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Poincare-type estimate controlling distance to the null space by an energy dominated by the objective certifies quotient coercivity.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\le C(1+E(x))\).
\(F(x)\ge aE(x)-b\) with \(a>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is coercive modulo }N.

notation.meaning: energy controlling displacement transverse to the invariant directions

knowledge_statements.title: Poincare-Type Quotient Coercivity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of ambient coercivity despite quotient control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(H^1(0,1)\), let \[F(u)=\int_0^1|u'(x)|^2\,dx.\] Then \(F(u+c)=F(u)\), and \(u_j\equiv j\) satisfies \(F(u_j)=0\) while \(\|u_j\|_{H^1}\to\infty\). Thus ambient sublevels are unbounded. After imposing \(\int_0^1u=0\), Poincare's inequality bounds the normalized representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative energy cannot control additive constants; mean normalization removes the escaping null direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is not ambiently coercive but is coercive modulo constants}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unnormalized Escape Along Null Directions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded normalized representatives for invariant functionals on a complemented quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=N\oplus Z\) with bounded projection \(P_N:X\to N\), and suppose \(F(x+n)=F(x)\) for every \(n\in N\). If \(F\) is coercive modulo \(N\), then every energy-bounded sequence \((x_j)\) has normalized representatives \[z_j=x_j-P_Nx_j\in Z,\qquad F(z_j)=F(x_j),\] bounded in \(X\). Conversely, boundedness in \(Z\) of every normalized finite sublevel implies coercivity modulo \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the null space is complemented, subtracting its component converts quotient coercivity into boundedness of normalized representatives.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a closed complemented subspace of \(X\).
\(F\) is invariant under translations by \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quotient coercivity is equivalent to boundedness of normalized sublevels in the fixed complement.

notation.meaning: bounded projection onto the invariant subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Complemented-Kernel Normalization Principle

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(N\subset X\) is a closed subspace representing null directions.
\(F:X\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is invariant under \(N\): \(F(x+n)=F(x)\) for all \(n\in N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coercivity modulo \(N\) is ordinary coercivity of the induced functional on \(X/N\), equivalently boundedness of quotient sublevels.

notation.meaning: Distance from an element to the invariant subspace.
Quotient map from X to the space of equivalence classes modulo N.
Functional induced by F on the quotient.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quotient coercivity is the canonical formulation of coercivity modulo null directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercivity after quotienting additive null directions such as constants, translations, or finite-dimensional kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The functional \(F\) is coercive modulo \(N\) when
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\to\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(x)\to\infty.
\]
Invariance makes \(\bar F(\pi x):=F(x)\) well defined on \(X/N\), whose norm is \(\|\pi x\|_{X/N}=\operatorname{dist}(x,N)\). Hence coercivity modulo \(N\) is precisely coercivity of \(\bar F\). Equivalently, for every \(c\in\mathbb R\), the quotient sublevel \(\pi(\{x:F(x)\leq c\})\) is bounded. If bounded representatives can be selected, normalized minimizing sequences are bounded in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional is coercive modulo its null directions when its sublevels become bounded after passage to the corresponding quotient space.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity Modulo Invariances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly formulates coercivity modulo an invariant closed subspace through the quotient norm, but no source is cited.

children.title: Sublevel-Set Boundedness
children.top_down_role: Boundedness properties of functional sublevel families in relevant topologies.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(F:X\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is an extended-real functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Level-boundedness means \(\{x\in X:F(x)\leq c\}\) is bounded for every finite \(c\).

notation.meaning: Sublevel set of F at height c.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness of all finite sublevels in the ambient norm.

source_refs.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c\in\mathbb R\), define the finite sublevel set
\[
L_c(F):=\{x\in X:F(x)\leq c\}.
\]
The functional \(F\) is level-bounded if \(L_c(F)\) is bounded in \(X\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R\). Equivalently, for each \(c\) there exists \(R_c<\infty\) such that \(F(x)\leq c\) implies \(\|x\|\leq R_c\). Empty sublevels are bounded by convention. This definition concerns boundedness only and does not itself require lower semicontinuity, compactness, or attainment of the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional is level-bounded when every sublevel below a finite height is bounded in the ambient norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Sublevel-Set Boundedness

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1.5 Boundedness of level sets p. 826
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate boundedness consequence of level-boundedness before any topology-specific compactness argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be level-bounded on a normed space and let \(m:=\inf_XF\in\mathbb R\). Every sequence \((x_k)\) satisfying \(F(x_k)\to m\) is norm bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every minimizing sequence of a level-bounded functional with finite infimum is norm bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space.
\(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is level-bounded.
\(\inf_XF\in\mathbb R\).
\(F(x_k)\to\inf_XF\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_k\|x_k\|<\infty\).

children.title: Coercivity–Level-Boundedness Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where coercivity and level boundedness coincide or diverge.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity–Level-Boundedness Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential coercivity versus level-boundedness on an arbitrary normed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The following conditions are equivalent:
\[
\|x_j\|\to\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(x_j)\to\infty
\]
for every sequence \((x_j)\subset X\), and
\[
L_c(F):=\{x\in X:F(x)\leq c\}\text{ is bounded for every }c\in\mathbb R.
\]
Equivalently, the first condition may be written as \(\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty}F(x)=\infty\). No finite-dimensionality or lower semicontinuity is required for this equivalence. Compactness of sublevels, however, requires additional topological hypotheses, such as finite dimensionality together with closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional diverges along every norm-divergent sequence exactly when each of its finite sublevel sets is bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(F:X\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is an extended-real functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequential coercivity condition \(\|x_j\|\to\infty\Rightarrow F(x_j)\to\infty\) is equivalent to boundedness of every finite sublevel.

notation.meaning: Sublevel set of F at height c.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Sublevels Need Not Be Norm Compact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional boundary of the coercivity-to-compactness implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an infinite-dimensional Banach space and define \[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&\|x\|\le1,\\+\infty,&\|x\|>1.\end{cases}\] Every finite nonempty sublevel is the closed unit ball, so \(F\) is coercive in the extended-real sequential sense and norm lower semicontinuous. Nevertheless, its finite sublevel is not norm compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator of the closed unit ball is coercive and lower semicontinuous but lacks norm-compact sublevels in infinite dimensions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is infinite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coercivity plus norm lower semicontinuity does not imply norm-compact sublevels.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Sublevels Need Not Be Norm Compact

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological upgrades of the accepted coercivity-level-boundedness equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be coercive. If \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(F\) is lower semicontinuous, every finite sublevel is norm compact. If \(X\) is reflexive and \(F\) is weakly lower semicontinuous, every finite sublevel is weakly compact. In either regime, a proper \(F\) with finite infimum attains its infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coercivity gives bounded sublevels; suitable lower semicontinuity and ambient compactness upgrade them to compact sublevels and existence.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is coercive.
Either \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(F\) is lower semicontinuous, or \(X\) is reflexive and \(F\) is weakly lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite sublevels are compact in the corresponding topology, and a proper finite-infimum functional attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Sublevel Regimes Beyond Boundedness

children.title: Reflexive Weak Compactness
children.top_down_role: Compactness in reflexive Sobolev and Lebesgue spaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness alone need not imply weak subsequential compactness outside reflexive spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\ell^1\), the unit vectors \(e_n\) satisfy \(\|e_n\|_1=1\) but have no weakly convergent subsequence. Thus boundedness alone cannot replace reflexivity or a separate weak-compactness criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bounded unit-vector sequence in l1 has no weakly convergent subsequence, showing the necessity of an additional compactness hypothesis.
assumptions_latex: \((e_n)\) is the canonical unit-vector sequence in \(\ell^1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((e_n)\) is norm bounded but not relatively weakly sequentially compact in \(\ell^1\).

notation.meaning: The nth canonical unit vector in l1.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonreflexive Boundedness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical characterizations of the reflexive compactness mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a Banach space \(X\), the following are equivalent: \(X\) is reflexive; its closed unit ball \(B_X\) is weakly compact; every bounded sequence in \(X\) has a weakly convergent subsequence. The sequential equivalence uses the Eberlein–Šmulian theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space is reflexive exactly when its unit ball is weakly compact, equivalently when every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ reflexive}\iff B_X\text{ weakly compact}\iff\text{every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reflexivity–Weak Compactness Equivalences

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a reflexive Banach space.
\((x_j)\subset X\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are a subsequence \((x_{j_k})\) and \(x\in X\) such that \(x_{j_k}\rightharpoonup x\).

notation.meaning: Weak convergence in the Banach space X.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded-sequence weak compactness in reflexive Banach spaces is classical
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak compactness of bounded sets in reflexive Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every bounded sequence \((x_j)\) in a reflexive Banach space \(X\) possesses a subsequence \((x_{j_k})\) and an element \(x\in X\) such that
\[
x_{j_k}\rightharpoonup x,
\qquad
\ell(x_{j_k})\to\ell(x)\quad\text{for every }\ell\in X^*.
\]
In particular, bounded sublevels of a functional on \(L^p\) or \(W^{1,p}\), with \(1<p<\infty\), are weakly relatively sequentially compact. If the sublevel is also weakly closed, then it is weakly sequentially compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every bounded sequence in a reflexive Banach space has a weakly convergent subsequence; weakly closed bounded sublevels are therefore weakly compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Reflexive Weak Compactness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is the correct compactness result for this leaf and is stated with sufficient hypotheses, but it lacks an inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm control inherited by weak-star limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_j^*\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}x^*\) in \(X^*\), then \(\|x^*\|\le\liminf_j\|x_j^*\|\). Consequently, closed dual norm balls are weak-star closed and weak-star compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The norm of a weak-star limit cannot exceed the lower limit of the approximating dual norms.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space.
\(x_j^*\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}x^*\) in \(X^*\).

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a separable Banach space.
\((x_j^*)\subset X^*\) satisfies \(\sup_j\|x_j^*\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Some subsequence converges in \(\sigma(X^*,X)\) to an element of \(X^*\).

notation.meaning: Weak-star topology on the dual X star induced by X.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sequential Banach-Alaoglu for a separable predual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak-star compactness on bounded dual sets when the predual is separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \(x^*\in X^*\) and a subsequence \((x_{j_k}^*)\) such that
\[
x_{j_k}^*\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}x^*,
\qquad
\langle x_{j_k}^*,x\rangle\to\langle x^*,x\rangle
\quad\text{for every }x\in X.
\]
Indeed, norm-bounded subsets of \(X^*\) are compact in \(\sigma(X^*,X)\); separability of \(X\) makes this topology metrizable on bounded subsets and therefore supplies subsequences. Without separability, weak-star compactness remains valid, but sequential compactness need not follow in this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded sequence in the dual of a separable Banach space has a weak-star convergent subsequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Star Compactness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separability hypothesis correctly supplies sequential weak-star compactness on bounded dual sets, but no source is cited.

children.title: BV Compactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical BV Embedding Is Not Compact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp endpoint boundary for BV-to-Lebesgue compactness in dimensions at least two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\ge2\), the embedding \(BV(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^{d/(d-1)}(\Omega)\) is generally not compact when \(\Omega\) contains a ball. Concentrating rescalings provide bounded BV sequences with no strongly convergent subsequence at the critical exponent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential weak-star compactness for uniformly bounded finite Radon measures on a compact metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \(\mu\in\mathcal M(K;\mathbb R^q)\) and a subsequence \((\mu_{j_k})\) such that
\[
\int_K\varphi\,d\mu_{j_k}\to\int_K\varphi\,d\mu
\quad\text{for every }\varphi\in C(K),
\]
componentwise. In addition,
\[
|\mu|(K)\leq\liminf_{k\to\infty}|\mu_{j_k}|(K).
\]
The metric assumption makes \(C(K)\) separable, so bounded weak-star compactness in its dual is sequential. This mechanism applies to distributional derivatives, fluxes, and concentration measures arising from energy-bounded sequences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BV Weak-Star Convergence Does Not Preserve Traces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary layers show that ordinary BV weak-star convergence does not imply trace convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Omega=(0,1)\), let \(u_n(x)=\max\{1-nx,0\}\). Then \(u_n\to0\) in \(L^1(0,1)\), \(Du_n\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}0\) in \(\mathcal M((0,1))\), and \(\sup_n|Du_n|((0,1))=1\), but \(Tu_n(0)=1\not\to0=T0(0)\). Trace continuity does hold under strict BV convergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact trace convergence in a subcritical target space under superlinear Sobolev bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The trace operator
\[
T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\to L^1(\partial\Omega;\mathbb R^m)
\]
is compact. Consequently, there exist a subsequence and \(g\in L^1(\partial\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) such that
\[
Tu_{j_k}\to g\quad\text{strongly in }L^1(\partial\Omega;\mathbb R^m).
\]
If additionally \(u_{j_k}\rightharpoonup u\) in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), continuity of the trace identifies \(g=Tu\). More generally, compactness holds in subcritical boundary Lebesgue spaces; the \(L^1\) formulation avoids endpoint distinctions among dimensions and exponents.

children.title: Equiintegrability Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria yielding uniform integrability of varying families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-bound criterion for equiintegrability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu(\Omega)<\infty\), let \(q>1\), and suppose \(U\subset L^q(\Omega)\) is bounded. Then
\[\sup_{u\in U}\int_E|u|\,d\mu\le \Bigl(\sup_{u\in U}\|u\|_{L^q}\Bigr)\mu(E)^{1-1/q}\]
for every measurable \(E\subset\Omega\). Consequently, \(U\) is equiintegrable in \(L^1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every uniformly Lq-bounded family with q greater than one is equiintegrable in L1 on a finite measure space.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu(\Omega)<\infty\).
\(U\subset L^q(\Omega)\) is norm bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is equiintegrable in \(L^1(\Omega)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) be a finite measure space. A subset \(U\subset L^1(\Omega)\) is relatively compact for \(\sigma(L^1,L^\infty)\) if and only if it is uniformly integrable, meaning under the convention of the immutable seed that it is \(L^1\)-bounded and its integrals are uniformly absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite measure space, equiintegrability is equivalent to relative weak compactness in L1.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a finite measure space.
\(U\subset L^1(\Omega)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform absolute continuity criterion for finite-measure-domain \(L^1\) families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A family \(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is equiintegrable if and only if it is \(L^1\)-bounded and
\[
\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists\delta>0\;\forall u\in U\;\forall E\in\mathcal A:\quad \mu(E)<\delta\Longrightarrow\int_E |u|\,d\mu<\varepsilon.
\]
On a finite measure space this condition prevents a uniformly positive amount of \(L^1\)-mass from being carried by sets whose measures vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equiintegrability means uniform boundedness in integral and uniformly small mass on all sufficiently small measurable sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Equiintegrability Criteria

children.title: Concentration Control
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms preventing localization of mass or energy on small sets.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is a finite measure space.
\(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is equiintegrable if and only if some superlinear convex gauge uniformly bounds \(\int_\Omega\Phi(|u|)\,d\mu\).

notation.meaning: Candidate family in the integrable space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: de la Vallée Poussin characterization of concentration control on finite measure spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The family \(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is equiintegrable if and only if there exists an increasing convex function \(\Phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) satisfying \(\Phi(0)=0\), \(\lim_{t\to\infty}\Phi(t)/t=\infty\), and
\[
\sup_{u\in U}\int_\Omega \Phi(|u(x)|)\,d\mu(x)<\infty.
\]
The superlinear gauge penalizes large values uniformly and thereby excludes concentration of \(L^1\)-mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concentration is excluded precisely when all functions admit a uniform integral bound under one convex superlinear gauge.
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The de la Vallée Poussin characterization fits concentration control and the representation kind, but it has no source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Tightness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Control of escape in measure or spatial variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Practical sufficient condition preventing spatial escape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a locally compact metric space and let \(V:S\to[0,+\infty]\) have compact sublevel sets. If a family \(\mathcal M\) of finite positive measures satisfies \(\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\int_SV\,d\mu\le C<\infty\), then \(\mathcal M\) is tight. Quantitatively,
\[\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\mu(\{V>R\})\le C/R\qquad(R>0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform moment bound for a coercive function forces a family of positive measures to be tight.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a locally compact metric space.
\(V:S\to[0,+\infty]\) has compact sublevel sets.
\(\mathcal M\) is a family of finite positive measures with \(\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M}\int V\,d\mu<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is tight.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercive-Moment Tightness Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Escape on a Bounded Open Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of automatic tightness relative to compact subsets of an open bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega=(0,1)\) and \(u_k=k\mathbf1_{(0,1/k)}\). Then \(\int_\Omega u_k\,dx=1\), but for every compact \(K\Subset\Omega\),
\[\int_{\Omega\setminus K}u_k\,dx=1\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\). Thus \(\{u_kdx:k\ge1\}\) is not tight as a family of measures on \(\Omega\), even though \(\Omega\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundedness of an open domain does not prevent mass from escaping toward its boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{u_kdx:k\ge1\}\) is not tight on \(\Omega\).

notation.meaning: Compact subset of the open domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Escape on a Bounded Open Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-measure form of the tightness–compactness equivalence on Polish spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a Polish space and let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of Borel probability measures on \(S\). Then \(\mathcal P\) is tight if and only if it is relatively compact for narrow convergence against bounded continuous functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For probability measures on a Polish space, tightness is equivalent to relative compactness for narrow convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is Polish.
\(\mathcal P\) is a family of Borel probability measures on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is tight if and only if it is relatively narrowly compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Prokhorov Tightness Criterion

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is measurable, possibly unbounded.
\(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial tightness criterion excluding loss of mass at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A family \(U\subset L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is tight in the spatial variable when
\[
\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists K\Subset\Omega\;\forall u\in U:\quad \int_{\Omega\setminus K}|u(x)|\,dx<\varepsilon.
\]
If \(U\) is also equiintegrable, then neither concentration on small sets nor escape of mass to spatial infinity can occur. On bounded domains, tightness is automatic when boundary leakage is not distinguished from mass inside the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightness requires the mass of every family member to lie uniformly, up to arbitrary error, in a common compact set.
knowledge_statements.title: Tightness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed spatial-tightness condition fits the leaf, but the claim that tightness with K compactly contained in Omega is automatic on bounded domains is generally false: mass may concentrate arbitrarily near the boundary. A sourced boundary convention or correction is required.

assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\) and \(\Omega=(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k\rightharpoonup0\) in \(L^p(0,1)\), while \(|u_k|^p\,dx\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\delta_0\) as measures and the energy densities are not equiintegrable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical shrinking-support sequence exhibiting concentrated energy despite weak compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1<p<\infty\), define \(u_k(x)=k^{1/p}\mathbf 1_{(0,1/k)}(x)\) on \((0,1)\). Then \(\|u_k\|_{L^p}=1\) and \(u_k\rightharpoonup0\) in \(L^p(0,1)\), but
\[
|u_k|^p\,dx=k\mathbf 1_{(0,1/k)}\,dx\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}\delta_0
\]
as finite measures on \([0,1]\). Hence \((|u_k|^p)\) is not equiintegrable, and its limiting energy contains a concentration defect invisible in the weak limit \(u=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded weakly null sequence can concentrate all of its energy at one point, producing a nonzero defect measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Defects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and content kind fit the concentration-defect leaf, but no source or locator is supplied for the weak-convergence and defect-measure claims.

children.title: Admissible-Set Sequential Closure
children.top_down_role: Closure families for boundary, pointwise, differential, integral, and geometric constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Closure Does Not Imply Weak Sequential Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional topology mismatch in admissibility passage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with orthonormal sequence \((e_j)\), and let \[A=\{u\in H:\|u\|=1\}.\] The sphere \(A\) is norm-closed, but \(e_j\rightharpoonup0\) while \(0\notin A\). Hence norm sequential closure alone does not preserve admissibility when compactness supplies only weak convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit sphere is strongly closed but loses feasibility along a weakly convergent orthonormal sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is infinite-dimensional and \((e_j)\) is orthonormal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is norm-closed but not weakly sequentially closed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Closure Does Not Imply Weak Sequential Closure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified closure mechanism for boundary, differential, integral, and geometric constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:(X,\tau)\to(Y,\sigma)\) be sequentially continuous and let \(C\subset Y\) be sequentially closed. Then \[A=G^{-1}(C)=\{u\in X\mid G(u)\in C\}\] is sequentially \(\tau\)-closed. Finitely many constraints are handled by the corresponding product map and product constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint expressed as the preimage of a sequentially closed set under a sequentially continuous operator passes to direct-method limits.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is sequentially continuous for the specified convergence structures.
\(C\) is sequentially closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G^{-1}(C)\text{ is sequentially closed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Constraint Preimage Closure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convex Constraints Are Weakly Sequentially Closed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core weak-closure regime for direct methods in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is a Banach space and \(A\subset X\) is norm-closed and convex, then \(A\) is weakly closed and therefore weakly sequentially closed. Thus \[u_j\rightharpoonup u,\quad u_j\in A\ \Longrightarrow\ u\in A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm-closed convex feasible sets automatically survive weakly convergent direct-method subsequences.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a norm-closed convex subset of a Banach space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_j\rightharpoonup u\text{ and }u_j\in A\Rightarrow u\in A.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Constraints Are Weakly Sequentially Closed

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a topological space and \(A\subset X\).
\((u_k)\subset A\) converges to \(u\) in the topology used by the compactness argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direct-method limit remains admissible precisely when \(A\) is sequentially closed for that convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract closure condition matched to the convergence supplied by compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The admissible set \(A\subset X\) is sequentially closed for a specified convergence \(\tau\) if
\[
(u_k\in A\ \text{for every }k)\ \text{and}\ (u_k\to u\ \text{in }\tau)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in A.
\]
Consequently, every \(\tau\)-convergent subsequence of an admissible minimizing sequence has an admissible limit. The topology \(\tau\) must be the same topology used in the compactness and lower-semicontinuity steps; closure in a stronger topology alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible set passes to direct-method limits exactly when it is sequentially closed under the convergence produced by compactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible-Set Sequential Closure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential-closure condition is mathematically appropriate for the leaf, but the record contains no evidence reference or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Lower-Semicontinuity Passage
children.top_down_role: Energy comparison between compactness limits and minimizing sequences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of the Energy Passage Without Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness and feasibility alone do not ensure attainment when the energy is not lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[0,1]\), set \(F(0)=1\), and set \(F(x)=x\) for \(x>0\). Then \(u_n=1/n\to0\), \(F(u_n)\to0=\inf_A F\), and \(A\) is compact, but \(F(0)=1\); the infimum is not attained because \(F\) is not lower semicontinuous at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimizing sequence can converge inside a compact feasible set without producing a minimizer when lower semicontinuity fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_n=1/n\to0,\quad F(u_n)\to\inf_A F=0,\quad F(0)=1,\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_A F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of the Energy Passage Without Lower Semicontinuity

assumptions_latex: \(A\) is sequentially closed for a convergence \(\tau\).
\(F:A\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is sequentially \(\tau\)-lower semicontinuous.
\((u_k)\subset A\) is minimizing and a subsequence satisfies \(u_{k_j}\to u\) in \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\in A\) and \(F(u)=\inf_{v\in A}F(v)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The energy-comparison step in the abstract direct method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((u_k)\subset A\) satisfy \(F(u_k)\to\inf_{v\in A}F(v)\), and suppose that \(u_{k_j}\to u\) in \(\tau\). Sequential closure gives \(u\in A\), while sequential lower semicontinuity gives
\[
F(u)\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}F(u_{k_j})=\inf_{v\in A}F(v).
\]
Since \(u\in A\), the reverse inequality follows from the definition of the infimum. Therefore \(F(u)=\inf_{v\in A}F(v)\), so the compactness limit is a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential closure keeps the limit feasible, and lower semicontinuity makes its energy no larger than the minimizing-sequence limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Semicontinuity Passage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct-method lower-semicontinuity passage is correctly categorized as a principle and is internally coherent, but no supporting source or locator is cited.

children.title: Tonelli Existence Theory
children.top_down_role: Classical and modern existence families for coercive lower-semicontinuous variational integrals.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Functional Analysis, Calculus of Variations and Optimal Control
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapter 16: Absolutely Continuous Solutions
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Functional Analysis, Calculus of Variations and Optimal Control

children.title: One-Dimensional Tonelli Theory
children.top_down_role: Existence regimes for absolutely continuous curves and first-order integrals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional compactness mechanism for derivative-coercive integrals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one endpoint trace is prescribed, then \(\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(a,b)}\le C(1+\|u'\|_{L^p(a,b)})\), with the constant depending on the prescribed trace. Thus a lower bound by \(c|u'|^p-C\) yields bounded Sobolev sublevels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing one endpoint converts derivative control into control of the entire curve.
assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\).
At least one endpoint trace is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_j\|u_j'\|_{L^p}<\infty\Rightarrow\sup_j\|u_j\|_{W^{1,p}}<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Normalization Supplies Curve Coercivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of full Sobolev coercivity for velocity-only energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F(u)=\int_a^b f(u')\,dt\) and the admissible class is invariant under \(u\mapsto u+c\), then \(F(u+c)=F(u)\) while \(\|u+c\|_{W^{1,p}}\to\infty\) as \(|c|\to\infty\). A trace, mean normalization, or coercive state term is needed for full-space coercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative growth cannot control additive translations of a curve.
assumptions_latex: The energy depends only on \(u'\).
The admissible class is invariant under additions of constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is not coercive in the full }W^{1,p}\text{ norm}.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Translation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural simplification for derivative densities of curves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite continuous \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\), Morrey quasiconvexity with respect to one-dimensional derivatives is equivalent to ordinary convexity of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For curve derivatives, quasiconvexity and ordinary velocity convexity coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is finite and continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is quasiconvex}\iff f\text{ is convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Dimensional Quasiconvexity Equals Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Autonomous Convex Tonelli Attainment for Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-endpoint autonomous curve integral with coercive velocity growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), \(I=(a,b)\), and
\[
A=\{u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb R^m):u(a)=a_0,\ u(b)=b_0\}.
\]
If \(L:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies
\[
c|v|^p-C\le L(v)\le C(1+|v|^p),
\]
then \(F(u)=\int_I L(u'(t))dt\) attains its minimum on \(A\). If \(L\) is strictly convex, the minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive convex velocity integral has a fixed-endpoint minimizing curve, unique under strict convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\) and both endpoint traces are fixed.
\(L\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\min_AF;\qquad L\text{ strictly convex}\Rightarrow u_*\text{ unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Autonomous Convex Tonelli Attainment for Curves

assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\), \(I=(a,b)\), and the endpoint-compatible class \(A\subset W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(L:I\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a normal integrand, convex in its last variable.
\(L(x,z,v)\ge c|v|^p-C(1+|z|^p)\), with boundary conditions or an added coercive term making the functional coercive on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functional \(F(u)=\int_I L(x,u(x),u'(x))\,dx\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercive first-order Tonelli existence for Sobolev curves with convex velocity dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb R^m)\) be nonempty and weakly closed. Suppose \(L\) is measurable in \(x\), lower semicontinuous in \((z,v)\), convex in \(v\), bounded below by \(c|v|^p-C(1+|z|^p)\) for constants \(c>0\) and \(C\ge0\), and such that \(F(u)=\int_I L(x,u,u')\,dx\) is coercive on \(A\). If \(F\) is proper on \(A\), then there exists \(u_*\in A\) satisfying \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper coercive one-dimensional integral with lower-semicontinuous integrand convex in velocity attains its minimum on a weakly closed Sobolev class.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Dimensional Tonelli Theory

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and local topic fit, but the exact lower-bound, coercivity, and lower-semicontinuity hypotheses require an authoritative Tonelli-theory source with a specific locator.

children.title: Scalar Sobolev Existence
children.top_down_role: Scalar multidimensional existence under convex-gradient structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness condition for derivative-coercive scalar energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a scalar admissible class has prescribed trace on a boundary portion of positive measure, or prescribed mean, then \(\|u\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C(1+\|\nabla u\|_{L^p})\). Consequently, a lower bound by \(c|\xi|^p-C\) yields bounded Sobolev sublevels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trace or mean normalization converts gradient control into full Sobolev coercivity.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) supports the corresponding Poincare inequality.
The class removes additive constants by a trace or mean constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_jF(u_j)<\infty\Rightarrow (u_j)\text{ is bounded in }W^{1,p}(\Omega).
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Poincare Normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp lower-semicontinuity boundary for autonomous scalar gradient densities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite continuous scalar-gradient density in the standard \(p\)-growth regime, failure of convexity is failure of quasiconvexity and permits oscillatory sequences that violate sequential weak lower semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex scalar gradient density permits laminating oscillations and loses weak lower semicontinuity.
assumptions_latex: The density is finite, continuous, autonomous, and has standard \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ nonconvex}\Rightarrow F\text{ is not sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous under suitable affine boundary data}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Scalar Gradient Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar multidimensional simplification distinguishing this leaf from vectorial theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite continuous scalar-gradient density \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), convexity, rank-one convexity, and quasiconvexity are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For scalar gradients, quasiconvexity reduces to ordinary convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite and continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ convex}\iff f\text{ rank-one convex}\iff f\text{ quasiconvex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Quasiconvexity Equals Gradient Convexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak lower semicontinuity with explicit control of state dependence and negative parts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_j\rightharpoonup u\) in \(W^{1,p}(\Omega)\), with \(u_j\to u\) strongly in a space controlling the state dependence. If \(f(x,s,\xi)\) is a normal integrand, lower semicontinuous in \((s,\xi)\), convex in \(\xi\), and its negative parts satisfy the required uniform-integrability lower bound, then \(\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\le\liminf_j\int_\Omega f(x,u_j,\nabla u_j)\,dx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex gradient dependence yields weak lower semicontinuity when state dependence and negative parts are controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\).
The Sobolev compact embedding used controls the state variable.
The negative parts are uniformly integrable along the sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(u)\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}F(u_j).
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Convex-Gradient Weak Lower Semicontinuity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar autonomous existence with explicit normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega)\) be nonempty and weakly closed, and assume that \(A\) has fixed mean or fixed trace sufficient for a Poincare inequality. If \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies
\[
c|\xi|^p-C\le f(\xi)\le C(1+|\xi|^p),
\]
then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)dx\) attains its infimum on \(A\). If \(f\) is strictly convex and \(A\) is convex, the minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized scalar Sobolev class admits a minimizer for a coercive convex gradient density, uniquely under strict convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonempty, weakly closed, and satisfies a Poincare normalization.
\(f\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\min_AF;\qquad f\text{ strictly convex and }A\text{ convex}\Rightarrow u_*\text{ unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Autonomous Scalar Convex-Gradient Attainment

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and Lipschitz, \(1<p<\infty\), and \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(f:\Omega\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a normal integrand and convex in its gradient variable.
\(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\) is proper, bounded below, and coercive on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u_*\in A\) such that \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar direct-method existence based on convexity in the gradient variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume that \(f\) is measurable in \(x\), lower semicontinuous in \((s,\xi)\), and convex in \(\xi\). If the functional
\[
F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx
\]
is proper, bounded below, and coercive on the nonempty weakly closed set \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega)\), then \(F\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous along admissible sequences under the stated normal-integrand hypotheses, and there exists \(u_*\in A\) with \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex gradient dependence, weak closure, coercivity, and lower semicontinuity yield a minimizer for a scalar Sobolev integral.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Sobolev Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar existence theorem fits the leaf, but normal-integrand status, lower semicontinuity, and convexity in the gradient alone do not transparently supply the asserted weak lower semicontinuity without appropriate negative-part or growth hypotheses. A precise source is required.

children.title: Vectorial Quasiconvex Existence
children.top_down_role: Vectorial existence based on quasiconvex lower semicontinuity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization Required for Vectorial Gradient Coercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction of the additive-constant gap in derivative-only vectorial energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lower bound \(f(\xi)\ge c|\xi|^p-C\) controls \(\nabla u\) in \(L^p\), but controls \(u\) in \(W^{1,p}\) only after translations are removed by a prescribed trace, mean normalization, or coercive state term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient growth gives full Sobolev coercivity only when translations are fixed or penalized.
assumptions_latex: \(f(\xi)\ge c|\xi|^p-C\).
The admissible class satisfies a Poincare normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_jF(u_j)<\infty\Rightarrow (u_j)\text{ is bounded in }W^{1,p}.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Required for Vectorial Gradient Coercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-One Convexity Is Insufficient in General
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Genuinely vectorial boundary between algebraic tests and quasiconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In matrix dimensions where rank-one convexity and quasiconvexity are known not to coincide, rank-one convexity does not guarantee quasiconvexity, sequential weak lower semicontinuity, or direct-method existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity along rank-one lines does not rule out every genuinely vectorial microstructure.
assumptions_latex: The matrix dimension lies in a regime with known rank-one-convex but nonquasiconvex densities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{rank-one convexity}\not\Rightarrow\text{quasiconvexity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Convexity Is Insufficient in General

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasiconvexity Is Necessary for Autonomous Weak Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity under affine boundary tests for finite autonomous densities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a finite continuous density with standard \(p\)-growth defines a sequentially weakly lower-semicontinuous autonomous gradient integral under affine boundary data, then the density is quasiconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak lower semicontinuity of an autonomous vectorial gradient integral forces every quasiconvexity test inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite, continuous, and has standard \(p\)-growth.
Weak lower semicontinuity holds under fixed affine boundary data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is quasiconvex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasiconvexity Is Necessary for Autonomous Weak Lower Semicontinuity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous vectorial first-order integrals with quasiconvex density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(1<p<\infty\). If \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and satisfies \(|f(\xi)|\le C(1+|\xi|^p)\), then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on \(W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous quasiconvex vectorial density with p-growth generates a weakly lower-semicontinuous Sobolev integral.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and open.
\(f\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_j\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }W^{1,p}\Rightarrow F(u)\le\liminf_jF(u_j).
knowledge_statements.title: Morrey Weak Lower Semicontinuity Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical vectorial gradient definition on a reference cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite density \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is quasiconvex at \(\xi\) if
\[
f(\xi)\le \fint_Q f(\xi+\nabla\varphi(y))\,dy
\]
for every \(\varphi\in W^{1,\infty}_0(Q;\mathbb R^m)\). It is quasiconvex if this holds at every \(\xi\). For finite continuous densities, an equivalent definition uses any bounded Lipschitz reference domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A density is quasiconvex when no compactly supported gradient fluctuation lowers the energy of a constant gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite; domain-independence additionally uses continuity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is quasiconvex}\iff \forall\xi,\varphi:\ f(\xi)\le\fint_Qf(\xi+\nabla\varphi)\,dy.
knowledge_statements.title: Morrey Quasiconvexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous vectorial existence with explicit translation control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) be nonempty and weakly closed, and assume that a fixed trace or mean condition gives a Poincare inequality on \(A\). If \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and satisfies
\[
c|\xi|^p-C\le f(\xi)\le C(1+|\xi|^p),
\]
then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)dx\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasiconvex lower semicontinuity plus normalized p-coercivity yields a vectorial Sobolev minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonempty, weakly closed, and satisfies a Poincare normalization.
\(f\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and has two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\min_{u\in A}F(u).
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Quasiconvex Direct-Method Attainment

assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and Lipschitz, \(1<p<\infty\), and \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, quasiconvex, and satisfies \(c|\xi|^p-C\le f(\xi)\le C(1+|\xi|^p)\).
\(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is proper on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u_*\in A\) satisfying \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autonomous vectorial existence under quasiconvexity and two-sided \(p\)-growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and quasiconvex, meaning that for every \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(\varphi\in W^{1,\infty}_0((0,1)^n;\mathbb R^m)\),
\[
f(\xi)\le\int_{(0,1)^n}f(\xi+\nabla\varphi(y))\,dy.
\]
If \(f\) has two-sided \(p\)-growth and \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed, then \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is coercive and sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on \(A\). If proper, it attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper vectorial gradient integral with quasiconvex density and p-growth attains its minimum on a weakly closed Sobolev class.
knowledge_statements.title: Vectorial Quasiconvex Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Quasiconvexity and p-growth appropriately support weak lower semicontinuity, but gradient coercivity does not by itself make F coercive in the full W^{1,p} norm on an arbitrary weakly closed class because constants are uncontrolled. The exact existence regime needs correction and a source.

children.title: Polyconvex Elasticity Existence
children.top_down_role: Determinant-sensitive existence regimes in nonlinear elasticity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical minors-based structure for nonlinear elastic energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A density \(f:\mathbb R^{n\times n}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is polyconvex if there is a convex lower-semicontinuous function \(g\) such that \(f(F)=g(M(F))\), where \(M(F)\) collects all minors of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A density is polyconvex when it is convex as a function of all deformation-gradient minors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=g\circ M\text{ for some convex lower-semicontinuous }g.

notation.meaning: Vector of all minors of the matrix F

knowledge_statements.title: Polyconvex Energy Density

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyconvexity Is a Sufficient Quasiconvexity Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural relation to the vectorial quasiconvex sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite densities under the standard regularity convention, \(\text{convex}\Rightarrow\text{polyconvex}\Rightarrow\text{quasiconvex}\Rightarrow\text{rank-one convex}\). The reverse implications fail in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyconvexity is a tractable sufficient condition for quasiconvexity.
assumptions_latex: The density is finite and has the regularity required by the standard implication chain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ polyconvex}\Rightarrow f\text{ quasiconvex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyconvexity Is a Sufficient Quasiconvexity Structure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Continuity of Minors Above the Critical Exponent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orientation-Preserving Polyconvex Attainment with a Determinant Barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supercritical polyconvex elasticity with a finite-energy orientation constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p>n\), let \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)\) be nonempty and weakly closed with a trace normalization, and let \(W(F)=g(M(F))\), where \(g\) is convex and lower semicontinuous. Assume
\[
W(F)\ge c|F|^p-C,
\qquad W(F)=+\infty\ \text{when }\det F\le0,
\]
and that \(I(u)=\int_\Omega W(\nabla u)dx\) is proper on \(A\). Then \(I\) attains its infimum on \(A\), and every finite-energy minimizer satisfies \(\det\nabla u>0\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive polyconvex energy with an infinite orientation barrier admits a finite-energy orientation-preserving minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(p>n\), and the weakly closed class has a trace normalization.
\(W=g\circ M\) with \(g\) convex and lower semicontinuous.
\(W\) is \(p\)-coercive and infinite when the determinant is nonpositive.
The functional is proper on the admissible class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ I(u_*)=\inf_AI,\qquad \det\nabla u_*>0\text{ a.e.}

\(f(\xi)=g(M(\xi))\), where \(M(\xi)\) lists all minors and \(g\) is convex and lower semicontinuous.

notation.meaning: Vector of all minors, including the determinant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplified polyconvex existence regime with supercritical Sobolev exponent and weakly closed constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(\xi)\) denote the vector of all minors of \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), including \(\det\xi\). Suppose \(f(\xi)=g(M(\xi))\), where \(g\) is convex and lower semicontinuous, and suppose \(f(\xi)\ge c|\xi|^p-C\) with \(p>n\). Then the associated functional \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(\nabla u)\,dx\) is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous under the corresponding weak continuity of minors. Consequently, if \(A\subset W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R^n)\) is nonempty and weakly closed and \(F\) is proper on \(A\), then \(F\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive polyconvex elastic energy attains its minimum on a weakly closed deformation class when minors pass continuously to weak limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyconvex Elasticity Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the polyconvex-existence leaf, but the weak continuity and integrability regime for all minors, and the resulting lower-semicontinuity assertion, need a specific authoritative source.

assumptions_latex: \(u\) is a Sobolev deformation with \(\det\nabla u>0\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \det\nabla u>0\text{ a.e.}\not\Rightarrow u\text{ is globally injective}.

\(A\) is sequentially weak-* closed in \(BV\).

knowledge_statements.title: Abstract BV Direct Method

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-growth existence in a reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) be reflexive, let \(A\) be nonempty and sequentially weakly closed, and suppose
\[
F(u)=\int_\Omega[\Phi(|\nabla u|)+V(x,u)]\,dx,
\]
where \(V\) is a convex lower-semicontinuous normal integrand with an integrable lower bound. If \(F\) is proper and a trace, mean, or state-coercive condition makes its sublevels bounded in \(W^{1,\Phi}\), then \(F\) attains its infimum on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reflexive Orlicz growth, weak closure, lower semicontinuity, and normalized coercivity yield a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is reflexive.
\(A\) is nonempty and sequentially weakly closed.
\(V\) is convex and lower semicontinuous in its state variable and has an integrable lower bound.
The functional is proper and has bounded sublevels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u_*\in A:\ F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u).

notation.meaning: Orlicz–Sobolev space associated with the Young function \(\Phi\)

knowledge_statements.title: Reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev Direct Method

assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) and its conjugate \(\Phi^*\) are Young functions satisfying the \(\Delta_2\) condition, and \(W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is reflexive.
\(A\subset W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is nonempty and weakly closed.
\(f\) is a normal integrand, convex in its gradient variable, and \(F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u,\nabla u)\,dx\) is proper, weakly lower semicontinuous, and coercive on \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u_*\in A\) such that \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev extension permitting nonsmooth integrands and non-power growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\) and \(\Phi^*\) satisfy \(\Delta_2\), so that \(W^{1,\Phi}(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\) is reflexive. Let \(A\) be nonempty and weakly closed, and let \(f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a normal integrand, possibly nonsmooth, that is convex in its last variable. If
\[
F(u)=\int_\Omega f(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,dx
\]
is proper, sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous, and coercive in \(W^{1,\Phi}\) on \(A\), then there exists \(u_*\in A\) satisfying \(F(u_*)=\inf_{u\in A}F(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct method extends to reflexive Orlicz–Sobolev spaces for proper coercive weakly lower-semicontinuous integrals with nonsmooth generalized growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Tonelli–Morrey Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Young-Measure Representation of Pure Oscillation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit bounded pure-oscillation family independent of the deferred gradient seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(-1<\alpha<1\) and define
\[
A_\alpha:=\left\{z\in C([0,1]):\int_0^1z(x)\,dx=\alpha\right\},\qquad
J(z):=\int_0^1(z(x)^2-1)^2\,dx.
\]
Then \(\inf_{A_\alpha}J=0\), but the infimum is not attained. There are uniformly bounded minimizing sequences generating the homogeneous Young measure
\[
\frac{1+\alpha}{2}\delta_1+\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\delta_{-1},
\]
so the loss of attainment is purely oscillatory and has no concentration defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous fields can mix the two preferred phases on finer scales and approach zero energy, although no continuous field with intermediate mean has zero energy.
assumptions_latex: The admissible fields are continuous and have prescribed mean \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{z\in A_\alpha}J(z)=0\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_{A_\alpha}J=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Field Double-Well Nonattainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dirac Young Measures Characterize Absence of Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic for pure oscillation when concentration is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_j\) be a \(p\)-equiintegrable sequence generating \(\nu_x\), with \(z_j\rightharpoonup z\) in \(L^p\). Then
\[
\nu_x=\delta_{z(x)}\ \text{for a.e. }x
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
z_j\to z\ \text{in measure}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With concentration excluded, the Young measure is a point mass exactly when the sequence converges in measure.
assumptions_latex: \(1<p<\infty\).
\((z_j)\) is \(p\)-equiintegrable, converges weakly to \(z\), and generates \(\nu_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nu_x=\delta_{z(x)}\ \text{a.e.}\iff z_j\to z\ \text{in measure}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degeneration of Strict Orientation and Injectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict determinant positivity and injectivity are not closed under strong matrix convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_n=\operatorname{diag}(1,1/n)\). Then \(A_n\to A=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\), while \(\det A_n>0\) and every \(A_n\) is injective, but \(\det A=0\) and \(A\) is not injective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orientation-preserving injective matrices can converge strongly to a singular matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A_n=\operatorname{diag}(1,1/n)\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_n\to\operatorname{diag}(1,0),\quad \det A_n>0,\quad \det A=0,\quad A\text{ is not injective}.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a topological space, \(A\subset X\) is an admissible class, and \((x_n)\subset A\) is a minimizing sequence for a functional on \(A\).
The sequence converges in the compactness topology to some \(x\in X\setminus A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The admissible class is not sequentially closed along the relevant minimizing sequence, and the limit \(x\) cannot be a minimizer of the original constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract sequential-closure failure covering boundary, orientation, injectivity, differential, and topological constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Loss of admissibility occurs when a minimizing sequence \((x_n)\subset A\) converges in the compactness topology to a point \(x\notin A\). The limiting point is then unavailable as a minimizer of the original constrained problem. Constraints such as boundary conditions, positive orientation, injectivity, differential inclusions, and homotopy restrictions require closure results in the chosen topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimizing sequence may converge to a point that violates the constraint. The resulting ambient limit is not an admissible minimizer of the original problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shrinking boundary layer can disappear in L1 and leave a limit with the wrong trace.
assumptions_latex: Admissibility requires trace value one at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_n\to0\) in \(L^1\), but the limit violates the prescribed trace.
